name: Solid perfume

lead: Solid perfume is fragrance blended into a wax or oil base, sold as a small tin, stick or compact. It is applied by rubbing a fingertip over it and dabbing onto skin.
Its appearance payoff is scent as part of overall presentation. Because it does not spill, it is the form people tend to carry in a gym bag or pocket for a touch-up after training or a shower.

paras: People apply it at pulse points such as the wrists, behind the ears and the neck, where body warmth releases the scent, as with other perfumes. A gym-bag-safe tin is the format forum users mention for use after showering at the gym.
Fragrance ingredients can cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. Wax bases can feel heavy on oily skin. Labels advise patch testing for sensitive skin.

angle.text: It adds fragrance to a grooming routine and travels easily, so people use it for refreshing scent away from home, for example after the gym.

lead: Solid perfume is a fragrance in solid or semi-solid form: aromatic oils set in a base of wax and carrier oil, usually in a small tin or twist-up tube. It is applied by hand to the skin rather than sprayed.

For looks and grooming, it adds a scent that people associate with being well kept. The format is valued for portability. In a 2008 gift-ideas thread on T Nation, one poster suggested solid perfume for a woman who trains because it will not spill and is safe in a gym bag [1].

General perfume references note that perfumers can dilute aromatic oils in liquid waxes such as jojoba or almond oil instead of alcohol, and that scent traditionally goes on pulse points where body heat releases it [2]. No clinical trials have examined solid perfumes specifically.

paras: Solid perfumes pair aromatic compounds with wax and oils. Perfumery references note that concentrations of aromatics in conventional perfumes vary by type, from a few percent in colognes to around 15 to 30 percent in extrait, and that terms for strength are imprecise [2].
Forum mentions are sparse. The one relevant example in gym-oriented forums is the gift suggestion for a woman who trains and showers at the gym, where solid perfume is recommended as spill-proof [1].
As with any fragranced product, individual reactions vary; irritation and allergy are the usual concerns.
